topic: AI's Impact on Search and Content Strategy
headline: Getting Your Product Into ChatGPT Isn’t The Hard Part, Getting It Through Checkout Is via @sejournal, @gregjarboe
keyNotes: Surprisingly, getting your products listed where AI programs (like ChatGPT) can find them isn't the main problem; the real challenge is making sure your online store's checkout can actually handle an AI trying to buy something.
Shopping done by AI programs is growing incredibly fast, with orders on Shopify through AI-powered search increasing 15 times since January 2025.
Unlike people who browse slowly, AI programs shop at machine speed, making many rapid requests, which can break online store systems built to handle slower human behavior.

AI programs often fail purchases not because they pick the wrong item, but because different parts of an online store (like inventory or pricing) might have conflicting information that a human could ignore but an AI cannot.
question: The article highlights that AI programs often get stuck when different parts of a system have conflicting information, like pricing or inventory. In your own work, where might small inconsistencies in data or processes cause a complete breakdown if an automated system, rather than a human, were trying to complete a task?
